elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.

elements.element: Customer has no minimum volume or usage commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any volume commitment, consistently with Section 12.3's disclaimer of any minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer is obligated to pay only for actual usage or Services ordered through an Order Form.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 limits payment obligations to Fees stated in an Order Form, permits usage-based pricing only where expressly provided by an Order Form, and prohibits unidentified minimum-use or similar charges.

elements.element: Any minimum commitment must not extend beyond the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: operative Section 2.1 eliminates minimum commitments entirely, so none can extend beyond the current 12-month term.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Section 2.1 imposes no minimum commitment requiring reduction; therefore an operative reduction mechanism is unnecessary.

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall must be resolved through a true-up.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: without a minimum commitment under Section 2.1, no commitment shortfall or true-up obligation can arise.

elements.element: No penalty may be imposed for reducing or failing to meet a minimum commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 eliminates the minimum commitment and therefore eliminates the predicate for any associated reduction or shortfall penalty.

result.reason: The operative redline replaces only the objectionable three-year take-or-pay provision with a direct disclaimer of minimum purchase and volume commitments. Sections 7.1 and 12.3 remain effective and consistent, limiting charges to Order Form fees or expressly agreed usage pricing. The fallback safeguards are satisfied by the demonstrable absence of any commitment, not by the non-operative margin comment. No unrelated commercial term is changed or contradiction introduced.
